correctness.rationale: For each fixed m, the standard Catalan recurrence for non-top Gödel implication values yields H_k=Psi_x^k(G) at G=(1−sqrt(1−4mx))/2. At r=1/(4m), square-root transfer gives the exact limiting survival product q_k(m)=prod_(j<k) d_j with u0=1/2, u_(j+1)=(u_j+sqrt(u_j²+h))/2, d_j=(1+u_j/sqrt(u_j²+h))/2 and h=1/m. This exact product is PRIOR, not the assessed new finding. Let X_j=u_j². The uniform expansion X_(j+1)=X_j+h/2−h²/(16X_j)+O(h³), with X bounded away from zero, yields X_j=(1+2jh)/4−h log(1+2jh)/8+O(h²) uniformly through m−1 by summing O(h³) local residual. Next log d_j=−h/(4X_j)+5h²/(32X_j²)+O(h³). Euler left-sum correction and exact integration give log q_k=−(1/2)log(1+2t)+h(4t+log(1+2t))/(4(1+2t))+O(h²), uniform t=k/m including k=0. At k=m−1, t=1−h adds endpoint shift h/3 and gives (8+log3)/12 as coefficient. Independent sympy series and integration check confirm all terms; direct product tests up to m500 have scaled error m²×max_k|error| around .207 to .228. They corroborate, but not prove, uniform O(m^-2). Limit order n→infty first, m→infty second is essential.

originality.rationale: Yildiz arxiv:2602.16135 (2026-02 v1, 2026-10-14 revised v2) explicitly derives the exact finite-m product and continuum leading q→(1+2t)^(-1/2). The revised full 36-page primary PDF was inspected, including its Part III Theorem 6 and proof: its orbit control is O(1/m) and logarithmic product o(1), with no explicit 1/m coefficient or uniform O(m^-2) remainder in the examined main results, appendices and numerical tables. Thus the new claim is a quantitative second-order refinement of already-known exact and first-order statements; no new exact finite-m law is claimed. Standard Euler summation is a method, but identifying and controlling the nontrivial discrete orbit correction is essential. Resultary related finite-chain papers concern different connectives/operators.
residual_risks: An unindexed supplementary numerical-analysis calculation could contain the same coefficient, despite absence in the 2026-10-14 v2 primary manuscript.

value.rationale: A uniform first correction to a natural full-Catalan logical truth-value distribution is a useful precise rate theorem: it quantifies finite-chain bias at every moving cut, resolves the top-atom side of approach to 1/sqrt3, and supplies a fully explicit coefficient with uniform O(m^-2) remainder. This nontrivial refinement is not merely reproducing the known exact product or leading continuum law, and future work comparing finite-chain sizes can use this exact rate.
